tasks.spec:
You are designing a live test plan for a text-message appointment-recall pathway that has just booked its first real appointment end to end. A human will execute your scenarios one at a time by texting a real phone. Your output is the test plan itself.

BOUNDARY. Everything is staged in ./sources/ in your current task directory. NEVER modify a staged file. NEVER run git, never call a network endpoint, never load skills or call MCP tools or Apps. The ONLY file you create is ./scenarios.json.

WHAT IS STAGED:
- STATE.md — what is proven working, the six known open defects, and the constraints that bound any test. READ THIS FIRST; the constraints are hard.
- v30_graph.json — the live graph: 22 nodes, 41 edges, seven webhook steps, seven globals.
- state-procedure-map.md — the design contract: eight patient states, five actions, nine patient replies, twelve numbered rules.
- approved-copy.md — the owner's copy rules, including banned words and the deferral behaviour for insurance questions.

YOUR JOB. Design the scenarios that would actually find the next real defect. The happy path is already proven, so a scenario that just re-books is close to worthless. Spend your budget on the paths that have never executed and on the ones where being wrong hurts a real patient.

Think about, at minimum: what happens when the patient asks for a different day and the search returns something that does not match; what happens when a chosen opening is taken between the offer and the booking; whether a reply that both selects and re-negotiates can slip through to a booking; whether an insurance question is genuinely deferred rather than answered; whether STOP and wrong-number behave honestly given that nothing is actually suppressed; whether the conversation can be pushed into claiming a booking that did not happen; and what a patient who replies in Chinese experiences.

HARD CONSTRAINTS, from STATE.md, that your plan must respect:
- A successful booking CANNOT be undone from the pathway side. Every scenario must declare whether it books.
- The test patient already holds one appointment, so anything that books creates a genuine double booking that a human must clean up manually.
- One conversation at a time, executed by a human on a phone.
- A conversation that reaches an end node is finished; further replies do nothing. So scenarios that terminate must be ordered accordingly.

WRITE ./scenarios.json AS A SINGLE JSON OBJECT WITH EXACTLY THESE KEYS:

  schema_version        string, exactly "mott-v30-scenarios.v1"
  scenarios             array of at least six objects, each with:
      id                short stable slug
      priority          exactly one of critical, high, medium, low
      title             one line
      messages_to_send  array of the EXACT texts the human should send, in order. Verbatim, no placeholders, no square brackets, no "insert X here". The tester types these literally.
      expected          at least 40 characters describing precisely what should happen, including which node should be reached where that is knowable
      failure_signature at least 40 characters describing what a DEFECT looks like, specifically enough that the tester cannot mistake it for success
      why_it_matters    at least 40 characters on the real-world consequence
      books_a_real_appointment  boolean, true if running it writes an appointment
      verify_where      where to confirm the outcome: the practice system, the gateway logs, or the message text alone
  recommended_order     array listing every scenario id exactly once
  sequencing_rationale  at least 60 characters explaining the order, especially which scenarios must run before any that book or terminate

HARD RULES. Do not propose a scenario whose outcome you cannot state in advance. Do not propose one that requires infrastructure that does not exist. Prefer scenarios that need no booking; where booking is unavoidable, say so and place it late in the order. Output valid JSON only, no prose, no code fences.
tasks.verified: every scenario carries verbatim messages a human can send, a stated expectation, a distinguishable failure signature, and an explicit flag for whether it books an irreversible appointment
